Sir Ernest Shackleton's crew play soccer near their ice-trapped ship The Endurance. Antarctica. 1915.

During an expedition to make the first land crossing of the Antarctic continent, the Endurance became stuck in sea ice in the Weddell Sea, Antarctica. She drifted northward, throughout the Antarctic winter of 1915. Eventually the ship was crushed and sank, stranding its 28-man crew on the ice. After months spent in makeshift camps as the ice continued its northwards drift, the party took to the lifeboats to reach the inhospitable, uninhabited Elephant Island. Shackleton and five others then made an 800-mile (1,287 km) open-boat journey to reach South Georgia, the nearest inhabited island. From there, Shackleton was able to mount a rescue of the men waiting on Elephant Island and bring them home without loss of life.
